tool.name: SelectRandomRecords

summary.para: Randomly or systematically selects features or table rows: a fixed number, a percentage, a sample size calculated from a confidence level and margin of error, a fixed number with selection probability proportional to geodesic area or length, or systematic selection (every Xth record, or all odd- or even-numbered records, in a sort-field order). The four standard selection methods are offered: Add to selects only from the currently unselected records, while Remove from / Select subset from the current selection treat the current selection as the population -- in every case before any calculation. Works on feature layers and standalone tables at every license level; an optional seed makes selections exactly reproducible.

tool.usage:
Selects a random or systematic sample of features or table rows, with ways to select that ArcGIS Pro's own random selection tools do not offer, and with no extension needed. The tool applies a selection to the input layer or table view (nothing is copied or created; follow with Copy Features / Copy Rows to persist the sample).
Sample-size methods: • A fixed number of records. • A percentage of the population. • Sample size calculated from a confidence level and margin of error: you say how good an answer you need and the tool works out how many records that takes -- the statistical sample size for estimating a proportion at a chosen confidence level and margin of error (Esri's tool calls this Auto Calculate): n = (z/m)^2 * p(1-p) with p = 0.5 (the conservative worst case), then the finite-population correction n' = n*N/(n + (N-1)), rounded up. Sample size barely grows with population (385 for a billion records at 95%/5%) but grows with the square of precision (a 2% margin needs about 2,400). • Proportional to area / length: a fixed number whose selection probability is proportional to geodesic area (polygons) or length (polylines), so larger features are proportionally likelier -- probability-proportional-to-size sampling. • Systematic: every Xth record, optionally starting at a random record within the first X (the classic systematic design; otherwise the first record), or all odd-numbered or all even-numbered records. Systematic methods walk the ascending order of the Sort field, which defaults to the ObjectID field.
An example of the calculated sample size: a season of camera trapping produced 12,000 auto-classified photos and you must report the classifier's accuracy. At 95% confidence with a 5% margin the tool selects 373 photos to verify by hand -- if 91% of those prove correct you can state 91% accurate, plus or minus 5%, with 95% confidence.
The population and the selection method. New selection selects from all records. Add to the current selection treats only the currently unselected records as eligible -- the sample is selected from them and joins the existing selection. Remove from and Select subset from the current selection consider only the currently selected records. In every case the population rule applies before any calculation, and to all sampling methods: a percentage is a percentage of that population, the calculated sample size takes that population's size as N, area/length totals sum over it, and the systematic methods walk it alone -- choosing even-numbered records under Add selects alternating even-numbered records of the current population of unselected records. (Removing 10% removes 10% of the selection.) Remove and Subset require an existing selection and stop with a clear message when there is none.
The analysis extent and polygon analysis boundary (feature layers only; both hidden for tables) restrict the population to features intersecting them (the default) or entirely within them -- both filters apply when both are given, and they combine with the selection-method rule (the population for Remove/Subset is the current selection intersected with the qualifying features). The boundary is a polygon layer from the map or a feature class from disk; a selection on the boundary layer is honored -- only the selected polygons form the boundary, and with no selection every polygon does. For the entirely-within test the boundary is dissolved first, so a feature straddling two adjacent boundary polygons still counts as inside their union. A layer's definition query is always honored.
Reproducibility. The same seed with the same inputs reproduces the same selection exactly -- cite the seed in a methods section. Every run also lands in Geoprocessing History with its full parameters.
Relation to Esri's tool. Data Reviewer's Select Random Sample offers the fixed number, percentage and calculated-sample-size methods (it calls the last of them Auto Calculate; the formula is the same) and takes feature layers and tables, but requires the Data Reviewer extension; this tool needs none, and adds the proportional-to-size and systematic designs, the four selection methods with their population rules, the analysis extent and polygon boundary, and the seed.

param.name: in_layer
param.displayname: Input layer or table view (a selection is applied to it)

dialogReference.para: The feature layer or table view to select from. It must be a layer (e.g. in the map) -- a bare dataset path has nowhere to show a selection.

How the sample size is determined: a fixed number; a percentage; a sample size calculated from a confidence level and margin of error (you say how good an answer you need and the tool works out how many records that takes -- about 385 at 95% and 5% for any large population); a fixed number with probability proportional to area/length; or systematic (every Xth, odd, or even records).
The number of records to select (fixed and proportional-to-size methods).
The percentage of the population to select (of the current selection under the Remove/Subset selection methods).

For the calculated sample size: how much the answer from the sample can be trusted. At 95, if sample after sample were selected this way, 95 of every 100 would give a range that contains the true share of the whole population. Raising it grows the sample modestly.

For the calculated sample size: how far the share found in the sample may be from the true share of the whole population, in percentage points. With 5, a sample that is 91% correct means the whole is between 86% and 96%. Halving the margin takes four times the sample.

param.name: sort_field
param.displayname: Sort field (systematic methods walk this order; defaults to the ObjectID field)

dialogReference.para: The field whose ascending order the systematic methods walk. Defaults to the ObjectID field; any integer, decimal, text or date field qualifies.

param.name: random_start
param.displayname: Random starting record (the first sample falls within the first X records)

dialogReference.para: Every-Xth only: start at a random record within the first X (the classic systematic sampling design, recommended), so the first sample is not always the first record. Turn off to start at the first record. The seed controls the start.
New selection replaces whatever is currently selected: every record in the input (within the analysis extent, when one is given) is eligible, and the sample becomes the new selection.

Add to the current selection treats only the records that are currently unselected as eligible: the sample is selected from those and joins the existing selection. This applies to every sampling method -- a percentage is a percentage of the unselected records, the calculated sample size takes the unselected count as its population, and the systematic methods walk the unselected records alone (choosing even-numbered records selects alternating records of the currently unselected population).

Remove from the current selection treats only the currently selected records as the population, samples from them, and deselects the sample -- removing 10 percent removes 10 percent of the selection. Requires an existing selection.

Select subset from the current selection also treats only the currently selected records as the population, but keeps the sample and deselects the rest -- thinning a selection down to a random or systematic sample of itself. Requires an existing selection.

param.name: extent
param.displayname: Analysis extent (optional -- only features in this area are considered)

dialogReference.para: Optional analysis extent (feature layers only; hidden for tables): only features in this area are considered part of the population.

param.name: boundary
param.displayname: Polygon analysis boundary (optional -- only features in these polygons are considered; a selection on the layer is honored)

dialogReference.para: Optional polygon analysis boundary: a polygon layer from the map or a feature class from disk. Only features in these polygons are considered. A selection on the boundary layer is honored -- only the selected polygons form the boundary; with no selection, every polygon does. Combines with the analysis extent when both are given.

bulletList.bullet_item: Intersecting the extent or boundary (the default).
Lying entirely within them; adjacent boundary polygons are unioned first.

param.name: random_seed
param.displayname: Random seed (optional -- same seed, same selection)

dialogReference.para: Optional: the same seed with the same inputs reproduces the same selection exactly. Leave blank for a fresh random selection each run.
Derived: the input layer with the selection applied (for chaining in ModelBuilder).

scriptExample.title: Select Random Records example (stand-alone script)
scriptExample.para: A statistically sized sample for accuracy assessment, reproducible with a seed, then persisted.
scriptExample.code: import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your install path # sample_method options (matching is by prefix): # "Fixed number of records" # "Percentage of records" # "Sample size calculated from a confidence level and margin of error" # "Fixed number, probability proportional to area / length" # "Systematic: every Xth record" # "Systematic: odd-numbered records" / "... even-numbered ..." # selection_method: "New selection" / "Add to the current selection" / # "Remove from the current selection" / "Select subset from the current selection" # extent_relation: "Intersecting the extent" / "Entirely within the extent" lyr = arcpy.management.MakeFeatureLayer( r"D:\data\study.gdb\veg_polygons", "veg_lyr") arcpy.jenness.SelectRandomRecords( in_layer="veg_lyr", sample_method="Sample size calculated from a confidence level and margin of error", confidence=95.0, margin=5.0, selection_method="New selection", random_seed=42) arcpy.management.CopyFeatures("veg_lyr", r"D:\data\study.gdb\veg_sample")

dataIdInfo.idCredit: Jeff Jenness, Jenness Enterprises (http://www.jennessent.com). In the same family as Esri's Data Reviewer Select Random Sample tool, with which it shares the calculation of a sample size from a confidence level and margin of error (Esri's Auto Calculate option, with finite-population correction). It adds probability-proportional-to-size and systematic selection, four selection methods, spatial filters and a reproducible random seed, and it needs no extension.
